title: Stand
description: The FINAL SET OF CHOICES a dying survivor gets, for one or more run-end reasons (M5 task T62 · FR-CBT-10 · FR-STY-07 · GDD Part IX "Canonical: the Last Stand" — death is a scene, not a card). Before T62 a death ended the run on the frame it landed and `availableActions` returned []; now `runEndReason` reports null for exactly one more turn, `sceneOf` prints this file's `opening` after the pre-T62 death sentence, and `standChoices` offers the strongest STAND_ACT_LIMIT acts the run can pay for, plus the engine's own unconditional floor act. Exactly one file per run-end reason (the graph builder refuses a second claim on the same reason, and refuses the two WINS outright — a won run closes on its project's own ending). AUTHOR AGAINST THE MEASURED SURVIVOR, NOT THE FICTION: at the frame the stand opens, measured over 102 stands in 160 runs (`measure/t62.ts --hands`), the player has 0.00 companions, has met 0.00 survivors, is at a held base 0.0% of the time, holds a weapon 5.9% of the time and a loaded firearm 0.0%, and is carrying 3.72 items on day 2.5 with a wound burden of 218.6. Two of GDD IX's own three example spends name a person, and neither person exists — so acts are a MENU, not a script: gate every act on something the run can actually pay for, let the unreachable ones be acts that never fire rather than branches that crash, and keep prose to what the engine actually does (`effect` is the only world change an act has).

requirement.description: An act's admission test. Every set field must hold; absent fields are ignored (the EncounterRequirement idiom from T47, the EndingRequirement idiom from T61). The vocabulary is closed and engine-side on purpose — content supplies prose and thresholds, the engine supplies the facts. The engine checks this object's keys against STAND_REQUIREMENT_KEYS at graph-build time in BOTH directions, because a typo'd key would make the act UNCONDITIONAL rather than fail loudly.

reasons.description: Deaths this act is admissible for. Absent means any death this file covers — and a file is already constrained by its own `reasons`, so set this only in a file covering more than one.

requiresCombat.description: Something is in front of you. Measured: 100% of `lastStand` stands, 0% of the three quiet deaths. Required by any act whose `effect` is `kill`.

minWalkers.description: Dead standing on your node. Measured at a stand: >=1 is 100.0% (A TAUTOLOGY — you are in a fight), >=2 is 56.9%, >=3 is 16.7%, >=4 is 2.9%. Use 2 or 3; 1 gates nothing.

minCompanions.description: Companions still standing. Measured 0.00 in 102 stands (T86's PL-M5-63) — an act gated here is authored for a future the game does not have yet, which is legitimate but must be declared, not assumed.

minMet.description: Survivors ever met. Measured 0.00 in 102 stands. Same warning as minCompanions.

minItems.description: Units in the pack. Measured at a stand: >=1 is 97.1% (NEARLY A TAUTOLOGY), >=2 is 84.3%, >=3 is 64.7%, mean 3.72. Use 3 for a gate that means something.

requiresAtBase.description: Standing in a base you still hold. Measured 0.0% of stands — PL-M5-69, and not fixed by T62: the stand reaches the `sacrifice` ENDING through an act's declared shape, not by making a fight at home possible.

requiresClaimed.description: A base was claimed at some point in the run (read off the log, so one lost on day 9 still counts). Measured 20.6% of stands.

minBurden.description: Untreated wound burden. Measured at a stand: mean 218.6, >=120 is 61.8%, >=200 is 37.3%, >=300 is 21.6% — against a LAST_STAND_AT of 80, which the survivor arrives 2.7x past.

minHumanity.description: Absolute standing, 0-100 (baseline 50). Measured range across 200 runs: 31-73 — the authored <=28 and >=85 bands are NOT reachable in play (PL-M5-70).

minDay.description: Measured: a stand happens on day 2.5 on average, and mortal runs end day 1-5. A threshold above 5 will not fire in ordinary play today (T61 shipped a minDays >= 8 that fired 0 of 241 times).

reasons.description: The deaths this file covers. The two WINS (escaped, held) are deliberately not in the enum: a won run closes on the finished project's own authored ending and there is nothing for a dying survivor's last act to be. The graph builder refuses two files claiming the same reason, because the second would be silently unreachable.

opening.description: The heightened line that opens the scene — what it is like to be here, printed immediately after the pre-T62 death sentence (which is byte-for-byte unchanged, so the authored death scenes are extended rather than replaced). This is the most important string in the file: it is what makes the moment a scene rather than a card.

acts.description: What the survivor can do with what is left. The engine offers the strongest STAND_ACT_LIMIT of these that the run can pay for, sorted by weight then id, then appends its own floor act ("Stop fighting it"), so this array is never the whole menu and never needs to cover the empty-handed case. Supply above the cap is the point: it is what makes two stands of the same death differ.

id.description: Unique within this file. May NOT be `stand.let-go` — that is the engine's own floor act and would be offered twice.

label.description: What the choice reads like on the menu. Imperative, short, and honest about what it costs.

text.description: What it reads like once taken. PROSE IS A CLAIM ABOUT MECHANICS (T61's sharpest audit lesson — four of its seven real findings were sentences simply false of the run they printed over): this text may describe only what `effect` actually does, plus the fact of being remembered, which the history beat makes true. There is no node-level item store in this engine, so `drop` text must not promise the pack can be picked up; a breach takes the base permanently, so nothing here may narrate a wall you patched.

shape.description: The ENDING shape this act resolves the run toward, read back off the Living History by sim/ending.ts. Absent means the run's shape is derived exactly as T61 derived it. SET THIS ONLY WHEN THE SHAPE'S OWN OPENING AND CLAUSES ARE TRUE OF THIS ACT: T61 could author "you went down at your own door" as the sacrifice opening only because the shape was unreachable, and T62 reaches it. Check content/endings/<shape>.json before claiming one — the audit found seven clauses in that file quietly assuming a base, and they had to be gated. NOTE WHAT THIS MEANS FOR REACH: `sacrifice` is declared only by acts in the lastStand file, so in the shipped set it is a LAST-STAND shape and a clause in ending.sacrifice.json gated on reasons infection/dehydrated/starved can never fire. Declaring a shape on a quiet death's act is what would change that, and nothing in the shipped set honestly does.

effect.description: The one world change this act makes, or absent for an act that changes no field anywhere (which is legitimate — saying a last thing changes nothing, and pretending otherwise is the defect above). `kill`: the thing holding you is put down, leaving a corpse and blood on the node exactly as any other kill does; requires `requiresCombat`. `drop`: the pack empties where you fell. `mark`: a note is pinned to the node, the same field the `pin` verb writes and the Map & Journal screen reads back.

weight.description: Higher sorts first; ties break on id so the menu is machine-independent. A non-numeric weight is coerced to 0 by the engine rather than being allowed to make the comparator non-transitive (T61's audit finding 6).
